question: Does busy waiting cause shared4 CPU regression?
conclusion: SQLite Java busy retries were zero. Bounded AQS reacquisition spin is directly sampled, but spin alone does not explain the regression. Controlled guard-scope/thread/carrier interventions and scheduler CPU/queue allocation evidence support an interaction between fragmented DB locking and VT rescheduling. No production lock change applied.

busy_counter_evidence.scope: DB.javaWaitObservations counts Java-side SQLite busy-retry sleeps; not a census of arbitrary native mutex calls

limits: Profiled modes change CPU/op; use stock cells for effect sizes, not profile percentages as an exact decomposition.
Source-line sample counts are not calls or exact time; inclusive stacks overlap; native SQLite detail is often unresolved into a library bucket.
CPU sample density differs by variant and profiler overhead is unequal; AQS and scheduler presence are supported, exact shares of the original +17.24% are not.
The prior reference used5M measured/1M warmup/4reps; this extended harness used2M/500k/3reps, so shared16 direction change cannot be attributed to worker count alone.
ThreadPark is not a complete census of ordinary unmounted virtual-thread waiting.
Outer-op changes guard scope and can also affect locality; it is a mechanism intervention, not a production-ready optimization.
Guest SMT topology observed but thread affinity/hardware counters were not controlled.
